name: Webwood Egg
summary: In Shadowthread Cave, Webwood Eggs lie in nests in Shadowglen. Naturalists seek viable eggs so they can study the young spiders in secure laboratories.

sections.title: A Contained Specimen
sections.body: A grown Webwood spider is venomous and too dangerous for one researcher to tame or subdue. So scholars like Gilshalan Windwalker collect unhatched eggs from clutches hidden in Shadowthread Cave. The eggs can be carried safely, and the spiderlings kept contained when they hatch. Naturalists can study them without facing the deadly fangs of adult spiders.

sections.title: Destined for Darnassus
sections.body: Teldrassil’s native wildlife has grown unnaturally aggressive and corrupted, alarming scholars across the boughs. Eggs and gathered venoms secured at Aldrassil are bound for Darnassus. Researchers hope that raising and examining the spiders in controlled settings will reveal more about the dark affliction spreading through the World Tree’s boughs.

faq.answer: Webwood Eggs are found in clutches deep in the tunnels of Shadowthread Cave, in northwestern Shadowglen.
Gilshalan Windwalker, a researcher at Aldrassil, wants the egg to study the aggressive arachnids troubling Shadowglen.

faq.q: Why collect an egg instead of capturing a spider?
faq.answer: A mature Webwood spider is dangerous and too massive to capture and contain easily. An unhatched egg can be transported safely and placed in a secure enclosure before it hatches.

faq.q: What happens to the egg after it is collected?
faq.answer: Gilshalan arranges for the egg and extracted spider venoms to be delivered to Darnassus. There, scholars can study the creatures away from the dangers of the wild.

angles.text: As a young kaldorei defending Teldrassil’s sacred boughs, you help scholars investigate the unnatural taint spreading through the World Tree’s native wildlife by securing these eggs.
As a druid, you can learn how tainted Webwood spiders reproduce and behave. That offers clues to healing Teldrassil’s disrupted natural balance.
